title: Testing Clustered Equal Predictive Ability with Unknown Clusters
abstract: arXiv:2507.14621v4 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: We develop tests of clustered equal predictive ability (C-EPA) in panels where the clusters are unknown and estimated by Panel Kmeans. Since the hypotheses depend on data-driven clusters, we adopt a selective conditional inference framework. We show that the square root of a Wald statistic for the equality of two estimated cluster centers is asymptotically a truncated $\chi$ variable, conditionally on the selected clusters and their number, with multiple random initializations, and that the truncation set is a finite union of intervals that can be computed exactly. Unlike existing methods of selective inference for Kmeans, this holds under serial and cross-sectional dependence and heteroskedasticity. For the C-EPA hypothesis, we combine the pairwise $p$-values with a test of overall EPA. In Monte Carlo experiments, the proposed tests control size where naive tests severely over-reject.
